title: Act II: Unfolding the Lunar Rover & First Drive

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Jim, let's step over to Quad 1 on the LM descent stage. Time to unfold the Lunar Roving Vehicle—first time humanity has ever deployed a vehicle on another world.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: Grabbed the deployment lanyard. On your mark, Dave. Pulling tape 'A' to release the primary latches.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: She's swinging out smoothly. The chassis hinge is engaging, and the rear wheels are unfolding automatically. Now pull lanyard 'B' to let the torsion springs lock the forward chassis.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: <color=#FFFF55>CLACK!</color> That sound through my suit glove was music to my ears. All four wheels are down and locked on the regolith!

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Look at these tires, Jim. No rubber or pressurized air—those would rupture in the vacuum or crack in the minus one-hundred-degree lunar night. They're woven zinc-coated steel wire mesh with titanium chevron treads for grip.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: And each wheel is powered by its own individual one-quarter-horsepower electric DC motor with harmonic drive gearing. Even if three fail, one can still roll us home.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Earth weight of the rover is 210 kilograms, but here in one-sixth gravity, she weighs only 35 kilograms! I can literally lift the rear bumper with one hand.

lines.speaker: Joe Allen (CAPCOM)
lines.text: Falcon, Houston confirms telemetry from the LRV battery systems. Two 36-volt silver-zinc batteries reading nominal voltage.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: I'm strapped into the left seat. Taking hold of the central T-handle controller. Pushing forward to apply power...

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: We are rolling! Look at the dust arching off the mesh wheels—like twin rooster-tails in slow motion!

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: She handles like a dream, bouncing gently over the crater rims. Cruise speed is right around nine kilometers per hour. Jim, keep an eye on our dead-reckoning navigation console.

lines.speaker: James Irwin
lines.text: Directional gyro and odometer are synchronized. Range from the LM: one point two kilometers. Bearing: two-zero-five toward Elbow Crater. Remember the flight rule: we must always remain within walking distance of Falcon in case the rover stops.

lines.speaker: David Scott
lines.text: Copy that. We have five kilometers of allowable operational radius, expanding our exploration zone ten times wider than any previous Apollo mission. Let's head for the rim of Hadley Rille!
